title: Arslanov’s completeness criterion

summary: A c.e. oracle computes a total function avoiding every fixed point on domain indices exactly when it computes the halting set.
abstract: The recursion theorem forces every computable transformation of program indices to preserve at least one program’s behavior. Allowing an oracle may make it possible to avoid even equality of domains at every index. Arslanov’s completeness criterion says that an enumerable oracle can do this exactly when it computes the halting set. Finite approximations to the oracle give convergent numerical guesses and a settling bound computed by that same oracle; a self-referential copying family turns the absence of fixed points into a halting decider. An explicit construction from a diagonally noncomputable function gives an incomplete, non-enumerable counterexample when the enumerable-oracle hypothesis is removed. Conversely, a fixed-point-free function yields diagonal disagreement through one fixed program compiler, so exactly the same oracles compute total functions of these two kinds.
